requirement_or_question: Byte identity of compressed output across codec versions or backends cannot be promised: zlib is silent on stability, zlib-ng and zlib-rs output differs (Fedora, .NET, Firefox accepted it for speed), hardware DEFLATE is non-reproducible, gzip header bytes (MTIME, FNAME, OS) vary, and platform deflate variance caused npm integrity mismatches. Keeping compressed bytes out of identity insulates identity from drift.

requirement_or_question: DEFLATE recognition: gzip by 1F8B magic with bounded header; zlib by CM=8, CINFO<=7, FCHECK (FDICT ineligible); any other non-fast chunk is attempted as raw DEFLATE. Empty or >16 MiB inputs are ineligible; preflate verifies with a 64 MiB plaintext limit; complete raw consumption, expansion bound, wrapper checksum and side data <=16 MiB are required. Raw-DEFLATE attempts on every chunk have unmeasured CPU cost.
implementation_evidence: reconstruction.rs:58-117, 216-272; planner.rs:1107-1113.
research_needed: Benchmark per-chunk recognition time on random, text and media chunks; false-positive raw DEFLATE parses.

Unix compares dev, ino, mode, nlink, uid, gid, size, mtime and ctime (directories also after recursion); the Windows predicate compares only length, mtime and an always-false executable flag.

requirement_or_question: Frozen legacy export wrappers: ZIP entries encoded STORE and raw DEFLATE (flate2 1.1.9 level 6), DEFLATE only when strictly smaller; tar.gz one RFC 1952 member, level 6, fixed zero header fields; tar.xz one XZ block, preset 6, CRC64 (lzma-rust2 0.20.0); tar.bz2 level 9 (bzip2 0.6.1).
